title: Finding Boundaries from Areas and Probabilities (Inverse Normal)

questions.text: The random variable $Z$ has a standard normal distribution, so $Z \sim \text{N}(0, 1)$. Find the value of $z$ such that $\Phi(z) = 0.90$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of $z$ such that $\Phi(z) = 0.90$.

questions.text: The random variable $Z$ has a standard normal distribution, so $Z \sim \text{N}(0, 1)$. Find the value of $z$ such that $\text{P}(Z < z) = 0.10$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of $z$ such that $\text{P}(Z < z) = 0.10$.

questions.text: The random variable $Z$ has a standard normal distribution, so $Z \sim \text{N}(0, 1)$. Given that $\text{P}(Z > z) = 0.12$, find $z$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find $z$ such that $\text{P}(Z > z) = 0.12$.

questions.text: The random variable $Z$ has a standard normal distribution, so $Z \sim \text{N}(0, 1)$. Given that $\text{P}(Z > z) = 0.75$, find $z$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find $z$ such that $\text{P}(Z > z) = 0.75$.

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{N}(50, 4^2)$. Given that the standardised score corresponding to $x$ is $z = 1.282$, find the value of $x$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find $x$ when $z = 1.282$.

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{N}(100, 15^2)$. Given that the standardised score corresponding to $x$ is $z = -0.674$, find the value of $x$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find $x$ when $z = -0.674$.

questions.text: The masses $X$ grams of snack bags satisfy $X \sim \text{N}(52.0, 7.0^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of $c$ such that $\text{P}(X > c) = 0.12$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of $d$ such that $\text{P}(X < d) = 0.12$.

questions.text: Journey times $T$ minutes by bus between two towns satisfy $T \sim \text{N}(68.0, 5.0^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: On 90% of days, the journey takes more than $t_1$ minutes. Find the value of $t_1$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: On 80% of days, the journey takes less than $t_2$ minutes. Find the value of $t_2$.

questions.text: The weights $W$ kg of luggage parcels satisfy $W \sim \text{N}(72.0, 6.0^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the cumulative probability associated with the upper boundary of the central 80% of weights, and find the corresponding standard normal score $z$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the interval containing the central 80% of parcel weights, giving your boundaries correct to 1 decimal place.

questions.text: The lengths $L$ mm of steel pins manufactured by a machine satisfy $L \sim \text{N}(100.0, 15.0^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the cumulative probability $\text{P}(L < 115.0)$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that $\text{P}(k < L < 115.0) = 0.30$, find the cumulative probability $\text{P}(L < k)$, and hence find the value of $k$ correct to 1 decimal place.

questions.text: The fill masses $X$ grams of cereal boxes satisfy $X \sim \text{N}(500.0, 24.0^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the mass exceeded by the heaviest 5% of cereal boxes, giving your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the mass below which the lightest 2.5% of cereal boxes lie, giving your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

questions.text: The masses $M$ kg of adult antelopes in a reserve satisfy $M \sim \text{N}(620.0, 45.0^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that $\text{P}(620.0 - w < M < 620.0 + w) = 0.92$, determine the area in each tail and deduce the cumulative probability $\Phi(z)$ corresponding to the upper boundary.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the value of $w$ correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the interquartile range of the antelope masses, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.text: The masses $X$ grams of freshly harvested citrus fruit satisfy $X \sim \text{N}(50.0, 8.0^2)$. Fruit with mass less than 46.0 g is graded as Small. Fruit with mass between 46.0 g and $c$ g is graded as Medium. Fruit with mass greater than $c$ g is graded as Large.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the proportion of fruit graded as Small.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that exactly 35% of the fruit is graded as Medium, find the cumulative probability $\text{P}(X < c)$ and hence find the minimum mass $c$ required for fruit to be graded as Large, giving your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: c
parts.text: In a random sample of 6 fruit, find the probability that fewer than 2 fruit are graded as Large.
